title: Digital footprint
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Digital footprint”, English Wikipedia, revision 1378190774; CC BY-SA 4.0.
modifications: Complete lead introduction excerpted. Wikipedia TextExtracts API removes HTML and reference markers. Chinese learning notes are editorial additions.
paragraphs: Digital footprint or digital shadow refers to one's unique set of traceable digital activities, actions, contributions, and communications manifested on the Internet or digital devices. Digital footprints can be classified as either passive or active. Passive footprints consist of a user's web-browsing activity and information stored as cookies. Users intentionally create active footprints to share information on websites or social media. While the term usually applies to a person, a digital footprint can also refer to a business, organization or corporation.

Digital footprints can have consequences for privacy, advertising, employment, and reputation. Online activities can produce information that is gathered, linked and analyzed by any group or other parties, which can be used for inferences to be drawn about people. Research on digital footprints has also explored the relationship between difference in access to digital technologies, and difference in people's capacity to manage their online data, and their role in digital inequality.

On one side, it is the subject of many privacy issues. For example, without an individual's authorization, strangers can piece together information about that individual by only using search engines. Social inequalities are exacerbated by the limited access afforded to marginalized communities. Furthermore, employers use a candidate's digital footprint for online vetting. Between two equal candidates, a candidate with a positive digital footprint may have an advantage. As technology use becomes more widespread, even children generate larger digital footprints with potential positive and negative consequences such as college admissions. Media and information literacy frameworks and educational efforts promote awareness of digital footprints as part of a citizen's digital privacy. Because digital footprints are difficult to avoid, scholars and policymakers increasingly emphasize the importance of understanding how online behavior can shape public perception and opportunities.

questions.prompt: 根据第一段，下列哪种行为最符合主动数字足迹的定义？
options: 浏览网页时留下访问记录
网站以 cookie 形式保存浏览信息
用户有意在社交媒体上分享信息
陌生人用搜索引擎汇总某人的资料
questions.explanation: 第一段将主动数字足迹解释为用户为了分享信息而有意留下的记录；浏览活动及 cookie 信息属于被动足迹。陌生人搜集资料是后文讨论的利用足迹的行为。

questions.prompt: 文章为什么说数字足迹可能影响求职机会？
options: 雇主会进行网络背景筛查，积极的数字足迹可能在条件相当时带来优势
网络筛查主要衡量求职者发布内容的数量，而不是内容形成的印象
数字足迹的价值在于能够替代候选人的工作能力和经历
只有求职者主动提交的网络记录才会影响雇主判断
questions.explanation: 第三段指出雇主会使用候选人的数字足迹进行 online vetting；当两名候选人其他条件相当时，数字足迹积极的一方可能更有优势。原文使用 may，没有作绝对保证。

sentence.text: While the term usually applies to a person, a digital footprint can also refer to a business, organization or corporation.
sentence.translation: 虽然这个术语通常用于个人，但数字足迹也可以指一家企业、一个组织或一家公司留下的记录。
sentence.analysis: While 引导让步状语从句，表示“虽然”，说明通常情况并不排除其他适用对象。主句是 a digital footprint can also refer to...，情态动词 can 后用动词原形 refer；also 承接前半句，补充术语的适用范围。applies to 和 refer to 的 to 都是介词。
